## Design note

The economy floor: always affordable, never fast. Sagging springs and worn dampers make it lean hard and bob over every crest, the old hard tyres squeal long before they let go, and the tired four needs every one of its 5800 rpm through a long-throw 4-speed with a slow shift. Flat out it buzzes on the limiter at about 150 km/h. It is what you drive after the impound took your real car — slow, but it tells you exactly what the weight is doing, so it is a surprisingly good teacher.

## How this car breaks

A thin late-80s shell with a weak passenger cell: modest crumple rails and light pillars mean a hard frontal reaches the cabin (Simulation lethality is high), but panels are cheap and everything bolts back on. Small radiator right behind a plastic bumper — nose taps overheat it quickly.

## Sources (type)

- manufacturer spec-class data for 1980s 1.6 L FF compact sedans (4-speed manual / 3-speed automatic trims)
- owner dyno sheets for high-mileage 1.6 SOHC carburettor engines
- tyre test data for aged (hardened) radials: ≈ 0.85 × new street grip, earlier and louder breakaway
- engineering tables (tire radius, ride frequency, disc/drum brake hydraulics)

All values are class-typical figures for the archetype, rounded; no single real vehicle is reproduced.

## Inertia

Box approximation about the CG, scaled for mass concentration (`k < 1`: mass near the centre, e.g. mid-engine; `k → 1`: mass at the ends):

```
I_roll  = k_r · m·(W² + H²)/12
I_pitch = k_p · m·(L² + H²)/12
I_yaw   = k_y · m·(W² + L²)/12
```

|---|---|---|---|
| roll | 407 | 0.80 | 330 |
| pitch | 1782 | 0.90 | 1600 |

## Engine

1.6 L SOHC 8-valve I4, twin-choke carburettor, worn (≈ 10 % down on its new rating). Class-typical late-80s 1.6 SOHC economy engine (~45 kW/L new), derated ~10 % for wear (compression loss) per owner dyno sheets of high-mileage examples.

## Drivetrain

4-speed manual with a tired second-gear synchro (slow shifts), open front differential. Layout **FWD**; front diff: open; rear diff: open. Drivetrain efficiency 0.78 (default 0.85): worn CV joints, tired wheel bearings and dragging front calipers; class-typical 0.85 minus ≈ 8 % for high mileage. Clutch capacity 1.30 × peak torque = 160 N·m. Shift time 0.70 s.

| Gear | Ratio | Overall | km/h @ redline |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 3.17 | 13.73 | 44 |
| 2 | 1.84 | 7.97 | 77 |
| 3 | 1.26 | 5.46 | 112 |
| 4 | 0.97 | 4.20 | 145 |

Final drive 4.33, reverse 3.17. Speeds use the driven-wheel loaded radius 0.279 m.

## Suspension

Springs from ride frequency, `k = m_s·(2πf)²` with sprung corner mass `m_s = axle load/2 − unsprung`; dampers `c = 2ζ·√(k·m_s)`, ζ = 0.18 bump, rebound = 1.5 × bump.

| Axle | m_s | f | Wheel rate k | Bump c | Rebound c | Travel |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Front | 299 kg | 1.15 Hz | 15600 N/m | 780 N·s/m | 1170 N·s/m | 0.16 m |
| Rear | 196 kg | 1.25 Hz | 12100 N/m | 550 N·s/m | 820 N·s/m | 0.17 m |

Round 12b ride rule (A): the file carries the derived dampers × 1.2 bump / × 1.6 rebound (rebound ≈ 2 × bump), after any tunes below: **1880 / 3740 N·s/m F, 1320 / 3670 N·s/m R** (bump / rebound).

Anti-roll bars from a roll-gradient target of 6.5°/g with 70% of roll stiffness at the front. Roll arm h − h_rc = 0.404 m (roll centres 0.08 m F / 0.12 m R). Required total K_φ = m·g·arm/φ = 36620 N·m/rad; springs give k·t²/2 = 15986 F / 12167 R N·m/rad; bars supply the rest as `arb_n_per_m = K_bar/t²` = **4700 F / 0 R N/m** (clamped at ≥ 0). Resulting gradient 6.3°/g, front share 68%. Bump stops 120000 N/m.

Alignment: camber -1.3° F / +0.0° R, toe +0.00° F / -0.15° R (+ = in), caster 2.0°.

## Brakes

Full-pedal line pressure 100 bar.

- Front: 240 mm disc, pistons per side 51 mm → A = 20.4 cm², r_eff = D/2 − 25 mm = 95 mm, pad μ = 0.35: T = 2·μ·p·A·r_eff = 2·0.35·100 bar·20.4 cm²·0.095 m = **1358 N·m**
- Rear: 200 mm leading/trailing drum, wheel cylinder 17.5 mm → A = 2.41 cm², drum radius 100 mm, brake factor 1.8 (includes lining μ): T = BF·p·A·r = **433 N·m**

Lock check at 1 g on μ = 1 (load transfer m·a·h/L): front needs 1147 N·m/wheel (capacity 1.19×), rear needs 287 N·m/wheel (capacity 1.50×).

`wp_vehicle` gives the axle `bias_front` favours its full `max_torque_*` and scales the other by (1 − b)/b, so `max_torque_*` holds the caliper capacity per wheel and `bias_front` acts as the proportioning valve: the rear is trimmed to the same lock margin as the front (ideal rear = T_f · lock_r/lock_f = 340 N·m), never boosted above its caliper capacity. Rear capacity exceeds that, so `bias_front` = T_r/(T_r + ideal) = **0.558** → delivered 1360 N·m front / 341 N·m rear per wheel at full pedal. Handbrake 860 N·m per rear wheel.
